title: Makeup Museum — Content & Inventory System Modernization
role: UX & Product Design (platform re-architecture + branding refresh)
goal: Unify CMS, inventory, and storytelling to support exhibits and e-commerce expansion.
summary: Object-based content model, reusable templates, editorial workflow (roles/permissions, publish gates), asset standards, and brand refinements.

Team: [X UX, Y eng, Z editorial]

sections.title: Goal & Constraints
sections.body: Create a single source of truth for content and collection inventory to support exhibits and future commerce—without interrupting live operations or editorial cadence.

sections.title: What I Led
sections.body:
• Org & Ops — Proposal, scope, timeline, budget, staffing; coordination with engineering leadership.
• Research & Insights — Editorial interviews; inventory audits; workflow shadowing; stack feasibility sessions.
• Product & IA — Object model (Artifact / Exhibit / Story / Event); taxonomy; CMS field specifications.
• Design & Systems — Template kit (landing / story / collection); design system starter; brand refinements.
• Delivery & Quality — Backend service design planning/validation; implementation specs; QA checklist; a11y standards.
• Stakeholders & Decisions — Editorial/engineering decision forums; release gates; publish policy adoption.

sections.title: Research & Discovery
sections.body: We captured editorial needs, audited inventory/meta hygiene, and tested stack options to reconcile authoring speed, asset consistency, and technical constraints.

sections.title: Mental Models → Content Architecture
sections.body: We defined key entities and relationships, validated public labels, and mapped editorial units to reusable templates to reduce production time and errors.

sections.title: Information Architecture
sections.body: Navigation and taxonomy connect collection objects to stories and events; CMS field specs enforce predictable authoring and asset reuse.

sections.title: Prototypes (Lo-Fi → Hi-Fi)
sections.body: We delivered admin/editor screens (mobile-aware) and public templates with responsive image handling and media guidelines.

artifacts.caption: Roles and gates visible in UI

sections.title: Operating Mechanisms
sections.body: Roles/permissions, publish gates, asset standards, and an editorial calendar with QA checklists keep production steady and on-brand.

sections.title: Outcomes
sections.body:
Time-to-publish decreased, error rates fell, and brand uniformity improved across pages; the system is positioned for future commerce.
